script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Second Chance Bakery

INT. SECOND CHANCE BAKERY - DAY

*JANE (30s, a quirky, neurotic baker)* stands behind the counter, icing a cake.

Suddenly, the BELL for the door jingles. In walks KAREN (40s, a disheveled woman, carrying a box).

KAREN
(surprised)
Oh! I didn't realize you were open. I thought you closed down.

JANE
(smiling)
No, we're still here! We're just making some changes.

KAREN
(sighs in relief)
Thank goodness! I used to love your baked goods. I haven't had a proper cupcake in ages.

JANE
Well, come in and try one. My specialty is the Red Velvet.

As Jane hands Karen a cupcake, the door jingles again. In walks BOB (50s, a grumpy man, carrying a folder).

BOB
(frustrated)
What's the deal, Jane? I thought you were closed!

JANE
(smiling)
We're not closed, Bob. We're just making some changes.

BOB
(sarcastically)
Oh, great. Another attempt at a "new direction."

KAREN
(defending Jane)
Bob, it's not easy starting over. Let's be supportive.

BOB
(rolls his eyes)
Fine. I'll give it another try.

INT. SECOND CHANCE BAKERY - LATER

Jane is putting the finishing touches on a cake. Bob and Karen sit at a table, chatting.

BOB
(leaning in)
So, what's the deal with the closure, Jane? Did you run out of business?

JANE
(sighs)
No, it was just time for a change. I've been feeling stuck in a rut for a while now.

KAREN
(nodding)
I understand. I went through something similar a few years ago.

BOB
(raising an eyebrow)
Really? I wouldn't have guessed.

KAREN
(smiling)
Yes, I lost my job and had to start over. It was terrifying at first, but I eventually found a new passion.

JANE
(intrigued)
What did you do now?

KAREN
I started a gardening business. It's been challenging, but rewarding.

JANE
(smiling)
That's amazing! Maybe I should consider a new passion, too.

BOB
(surprised)
Really? What would you do?

JANE
I've always loved painting. Maybe I could start selling my artwork.

INT. SECOND CHANCE BAKERY - NIGHT

Jane is packing up her things, ready to go home. Bob and Karen help her clean up.

BOB
(putting on his coat)
Well, I guess I'll see you both tomorrow.

KAREN
(smiling)
Yes, and maybe we can brainstorm some ideas for Jane's new venture.

BOB
(rolling his eyes)
Fine. I'll play along.

As they leave, Jane sits at the counter, looking at a blank canvas.

FADE OUT.

Title: The Second Chance Bakery (CONT'D)

INT. SECOND CHANCE BAKERY - NEXT DAY

Jane is painting a scene of the bakery. Bob and Karen enter, carrying a box of supplies.

BOB
(laughing)
Looks like you've found a new passion.

JANE
(smiling)
I'm giving it a try.

KAREN
(encouragingly)
That's the spirit!

INT. SECOND CHANCE BAKERY - LATER

The bell jingles as customers enter. Bob, Karen, and Jane serve them, working together seamlessly.

JANE
(whispering to Karen)
I never thought I could be so happy here.

KAREN
(smiling)
Sometimes all it takes is a second chance.

BOB
(laughing)
And a little bit of patience from us.

INT. SECOND CHANCE BAKERY - EVENING

Jane is packing up her things, ready to go home. Bob and Karen help her clean up.

BOB
(putting on his coat)
Well, I guess I'll see you both tomorrow.

KAREN
(smiling)
Yes, and maybe we can start a painting class for customers.

BOB
(raising an eyebrow)
Are you sure about that?

JANE
(confidently)
Absolutely.

As they leave, Jane sits at the counter, looking at the new painting she started that day.

FADE OUT.

Title: The Second Chance Bakery (END)

INT. SECOND CHANCE BAKERY - NEXT DAY

The bell jingles as customers enter. Bob, Karen, and Jane serve them, smiling and working together.

JANE
(whispering to Karen)
I never thought I could be so happy here.

KAREN
(smiling)
And we're all here to support you.

BOB
(grinning)
Plus, the cupcakes are still delicious.

They all laugh as they continue serving the customers.

FADE OUT.

THE END
